TITLE: Siemens Q4 FY2026: record orders, higher targets, full price
QUOTE: We see significant opportunities ahead. Driven by powerful secular growth trends and the strengths of our core markets, we are raising our mid-term targets.
QUOTE_WHO: Roland Busch, CEO, Q4 FY2026 earnings call, 12 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: Siemens supplies factory automation and software, electrification, building technology and rail systems, and controls Siemens Healthineers. Fiscal 2026 revenue EUR 83.4bn; Frankfurt-listed, market value about EUR 220bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Q4 orders EUR 34.8bn, 29% above consensus; industrial profit EUR 3.9bn, 5% ahead, at a 16.8% margin.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: Mid-term revenue growth target lifted to 7% to 11% from 6% to 9%; EPS growth now double digit.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Mobility’s record orders convert mostly after fiscal 2028; China automation orders softened in September.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 21.6x forward earnings, 43% above the 2015 to 2026 average of 15.1x: the quality is priced.

H_P1: Orders reset the growth path, not the rating
P1_PARAGRAPH: Orders beat consensus by 29% and industrial profit by 5%, and the shares rose about 3% in early trading on 12 November, with the DAX higher. What changes is the growth path: management lifted the mid-term revenue target to 7% to 11% and EPS growth to double digit, backed by a data centre backlog above EUR 7bn and record free cash flow of EUR 12.1bn.
C1_TITLE: SIE: Q4 FY2026 results vs. consensus
C1_SUB: Reported vs. consensus, % · Consensus: analyst estimates before the release · Free cash flow: fiscal year; other lines: fiscal Q4
C1_COMMENT: The orders beat is large but mixed in quality: Mobility booked more than EUR 10bn, much of it long-dated rolling stock and service contracts, while Smart Infrastructure orders rose 39% on data centres. Revenue was only 1% ahead, so the profit beat came from margins, led by Digital Industries at 21.9% before severance.
BASE_CASE: Siemens has moved from a cyclical recovery story to a structural growth one. We underwrite fiscal 2027 EPS of EUR 10.20 to 10.80 excluding Healthineers, up 13% at the midpoint, with upside if US and China automation keep their pace. The case remains constructive, but at 21.6x forward earnings the risk/reward is balanced: further gains need upgrades, not a higher multiple. The next tests are the 10 December spin-off report, setting out how Siemens shareholders receive Healthineers shares, and the February votes approving it.
UPSIDE: Digital Industries Q1 growth inside its 8% to 12% range despite October pre-buying; data centre orders rising again in fiscal 2027; the EPS guide raised at the half year in May.
DOWNSIDE: Data centre orders stalling for two quarters on power access or permits; China automation slowing once price-led pre-buying fades; the Healthineers spin-off slipping beyond the planned May 2027 date.
H_A1: Results: margins carried the profit beat
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Comparable revenue rose 10% to EUR 23.7bn and industrial business profit 22% to EUR 3.9bn, a 16.8% margin, 150bp higher year on year. Digital Industries did most of the margin work: orders rose 15% and revenue 10%, and the margin before severance reached 21.9% on automation volumes, a better mix and some currency help, with software revenue and annual recurring revenue both up 12%. Smart Infrastructure grew revenue 15% at a 20.3% margin, of which 50bp came from US tariff refunds, a one-off we strip from the run rate. Mobility’s 9.5% margin reflected a favourable mix, and quarterly free cash flow reached EUR 5.6bn.

Surprise and reaction are aligned, but the move is modest for a 29% orders beat: the shares rose about 3% in early trading on 12 November, with the DAX also higher. Two confirmed facts temper the headline. Mobility’s record orders convert progressively, with many projects starting only beyond fiscal 2028, and China automation orders, up 8%, softened in September, while October was lifted by buying ahead of announced price increases. We think positioning also played a part: the shares traded at 20.2x forward earnings into the print, against a 15.1x average since 2015, so the beat confirms rather than changes the expected path.
H_A2: Outlook: a 13% EPS step without Healthineers
A2_PARAGRAPH: For fiscal 2027, excluding Siemens Healthineers, Siemens guides comparable revenue growth of 9% to 11%, a book-to-bill above 1 and EPS before purchase price allocation of EUR 10.20 to 10.80, up 13% at the midpoint. Digital Industries 8% to 12% at a 20% to 22% margin; Smart Infrastructure 11% to 13% at 19.5% to 20.5%, carried by electrification; Mobility 6% to 8% at 8% to 10%, held back by Mermec integration costs. Management expects about 70% of the data centre backlog to convert in fiscal 2027. In late spring 2027 Siemens will hand a 34.1% Healthineers stake directly to its shareholders, one Healthineers share for every two Siemens shares.
H_C2: Valuation: earnings must now do the work
C2_TITLE: SIE: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, Jun 2015 to 12 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus EPS, includes Healthineers · 40-week MA · log scale · last price is a results-day level
C2_COMMENT: Over 12 months the share price rose 19% against 13% for consensus EPS: the 12m-forward P/E stands at 21.6x, 43% above its 15.1x average since 2015 and close to the 23.1x peak of July 2026, with the price 9% above its 40-week moving average. Since early August, EPS rose 3% while the price was broadly flat, a mild derating. At the long-run average multiple the price would be about EUR 197, and a 10% upgrade at an unchanged price still leaves 19.6x. Consensus includes Healthineers, so the series will reset once the stake is reported as discontinued.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, Siemens Q4 FY2026 earnings release and call of 12 November 2026, analyst research notes of 12 November 2026
